note: Miller proposes sexual selection as a major origin of human mental capacities. Susan Healy's comparative review in Adaptation and the Brain, chapter 7, finds generally unsupportive evidence for the sexual-brain hypothesis. This challenges the central evolutionary reconstruction, not sexual selection itself. Miller's proposal and qualifications provide the substantive defense; they do not supply the missing comparative support. V9 applies to the foundational inference. Distinct evolutionary examples add learning, but do not independently validate that inference. Counterfactual assessment, low quality and density confidence; broad evolutionary account has no single historical endpoint.

Cognitive explanation of the transmission and recurrence of religious beliefs, rather than a defense or refutation of doctrinal truth. V8 is not established by the religious subject alone. Recurring mental patterns and cross-cultural comparisons offer transferable models. Description-only density estimate is low confidence. No high-confidence foundational criticism established in this review; no veto inferred from contested subject matter. No single historical endpoint or thematic deduction.

Institutional history links legal forms to capital accumulation. Salim Rashid's detailed review challenges the central causal inference: the magnitude of transaction costs is not established, small partnerships do not establish aggregate capital limits, and the counterfactual is not demonstrated. This is a foundational objection, not disagreement with a policy conclusion. Kuran's defense emphasizes initially adaptive institutions and path dependence; useful legal history survives the objection but does not resolve it. V9 counterfactual retains that payload. Finance and capital organization central, T12 applies. Core comparison ends around 1800, low endpoint confidence.

title: Foragers, Farmers, and Fossil Fuels
note: Energy regimes are proposed as drivers of moral values. Alberto Bisin's Journal of Economic Literature review praises the historical knowledge but directly rejects the convincingness of the central causal explanation. The book includes critical responses and Morris's reply; debate and valuable cases do not independently establish causation. V9 concerns this foundation, not the validity of all examples. Moral philosophy is the outcome being explained, T12 applies. Broad cross-period comparison, H13 zero. Description and review support only low-confidence density estimates.

title: Another Day of Life
author: Ryszard Kapuściński
note: Reportage from Angola's 1975 war offers observations about fragmented authority, communication and survival under conflict. These constraints give some transfer beyond local personalities; no high-confidence V3 established. Literary reconstruction limits evidential confidence. Factual criticism of a different book is not automatically applied here. Single-country war receives both thematic deductions. Density confidence low; war endpoint 1975.

title: The Emperor
author: Ryszard Kapuściński
note: Historian Harold Marcus documents material errors in the central court portrait, including claims about Selassie's literacy, teachers and written instructions. Literary or political allegory is a defense of artistic value, not accuracy of a work presented as reportage. V1 applies; do not relabel the source book fiction. Literary clarity remains in the counterfactual score. Ethiopia-centered political biography receives both deductions; endpoint 1974. Quality and density confidence low, veto confidence high.

Rosenberg argues that narrative history rests on a false theory of mind. Mariana Imaz-Sheinbaum and Paul Roth directly challenge the three central premises, including the inference from neuroscience to elimination of beliefs and desires as causes. The author's interview defends the eliminativist premise but does not resolve these objections. V9 applies to the foundation, not a minor historical detail. Counterfactual preserves useful methodological questions. Philosophy central, T12 applies; no historical endpoint. Description/review-based density confidence low.

title: Quantum Computing: From Colossus to Qubits
note: General historical and conceptual account, not a quantum-computing course. Originally Computing with Quantum Cats (2013); the renamed edition does not restart publication age. Physical computing constraints offer useful mechanisms, though popular physics is less novel for this reader. Everett interpretation should not be treated as proved by computational performance; reduced evidence confidence reflects that distinction. No high-confidence veto established. Broad development without one historical endpoint. Description-based density confidence low.
